name: The Rival Mob
label: Revelation
lede: Brendan Radigan, drummer of the powerviolence band [[Mind Eraser]], picked up a microphone in 2007 and fronted a Boston band that played late-'80s hardcore like nobody had told them it was over.

eras.title: Boston, by way of 1989
eras.text: Brendan Radigan and Justin DeTore started The Rival Mob to play late-'80s hardcore straight, with Breakdown, Rest in Pieces, Youth of Today and Warzone as the models. Two 7"s on small labels made them the Boston band people on the hardcore message boards were talking about.

years.cap: The Rival Mob at Anchors Up, Haverhill, Massachusetts, March 6, 2009
years.h: Mind Eraser's drummer starts a band and takes the mic
years.p: Radigan sings this time, with [[Justin DeTore|9baaa39f-4c99-4a6f-9537-e06c18c40ac7]] beside him. The first demo comes out the same year.
years.xp:
Members came over from Mind Eraser, Free Spirit, Mental, Righteous Jams, The Wrong Side, Xfilesx and more. Revelation later wrote that the demo was inspired by the 1987 Breakdown sound.

The band summed itself up in a Legends Arising interview: "NYC meets BOSTON meets CLEVO in 1989." The influence list there runs from Breakdown and Rest in Pieces to Slapshot, Murphy's Law, Carnivore and Fleetwood Mac.

yt: Raw Life live at Sound and Fury, July 22, 2012
years.h: Raw Life 7" comes out on Lockin' Out Records
years.p: Chris Corry records and mixes it at the Pain Cave. The first press is 700 on black, and the B-side covers fellow Boston hardcore band Down But Not Out.
years.xp: The year is a judgment call: IDIOTEQ's label history puts the EP in late 2008, while Discogs and ALARM say 2009. A clip of the band playing Raw Life at Sound and Fury in July 2012 is below.

years.h: Six songs, and a reviewer thinks of Sepultura
years.p: Hardcore for Hardcore arrives on Six Feet Under Records. ALARM's Todd Nief hears heaviness built from switches of emphasis and syncopation, not chugging.
years.xp:
Nief compared the effect to Sepultura and Black Flag. He called the singer's delivery "idiosyncratic and engaging," said the song structures were predictable, and ranked the band among the most deserving hyped hardcore bands since No Warning in the early 2000s.

Below, a full set filmed by hate5six on August 15, 2009, a year before the EP.

eras.title: Caveman steroids
eras.text: Revelation, the label behind the New York records The Rival Mob were chasing, signed them for a first album.

years.cap: The Rival Mob at Chaos in Tejas, Austin, June 3, 2012
years.h: Revelation signs The Rival Mob and promises caveman steroids
years.p: The label's announcement calls the Mob formula "the raw meat and potatoes" version, pumped full of steroids. Not for the faint of heart or the faint of pit.
years.xp: The announcement ran on May 30, 2012. It lists the band's history: a demo, Raw Life and Hardcore for Hardcore, with Breakdown, Rest in Pieces, Youth of Today and Crippled Youth as the touchstones.

years.h: Full set filmed by hate5six, August 11, 2012
yt: Full set filmed by hate5six, August 11, 2012

years.src: Discogs · Revelation Records · Legends Arising · Hardcore Punk Wiki
yt: Full set, August 11, 2012, six months before the album
years.p: Twelve songs from Intro Grunt to Thought Control, recorded and mixed by guitarist Trevor Vaughan. Revelation presses 1,095 on gold, 655 on black and 438 on seafoam green.
years.xp:
Brendan Radigan sings, Trevor Vaughan and Doug Free play guitar, Pearse McGrath plays bass. Legends Arising made it album of the month for March 2013, and a Hardcore Punk Wiki rundown of the Revelation catalog called it a love letter to the old Boston hardcore scene.

That wiki counts 3,000 to 4,000 copies across three or four pressings, and calls it pretty easy to collect and affordable.

eras.title: We never break up
eras.text: The Rival Mob played the big hardcore festivals (This Is Hardcore, Sound and Fury, Chaos in Tejas) and flew to Sweden for one show. Radigan was laid off, busy with other bands, and the new 7" never came out.

years.cap: The Rival Mob at Chaos in Tejas, Austin, June 3, 2012
yt: Full set, This Is Hardcore, July 26, 2015
years.h: Back from Sweden, The Rival Mob play Webster Hall
years.p: New York's Black N' Blue Bowl books the band for May 16-17, with a new 7" written but not recorded and one new song set to debut.
years.xp:
Radigan told Vice it was "surreal" that anyone would put the band on a plane for one show in Sweden. He had played Webster Hall before, at Sheer Terror's comeback show, and was glad to finally be asked back.

This Is Hardcore and a California show were next. Below, the full set hate5six filmed at This Is Hardcore on July 26, 2015.

years.p: Radigan told Vice the band goes "super super dormant" rather than splitting. He was also in Mind Eraser, Battle Ruins, Stone Dagger and [[Magic Circle|688fe3f7-3a4c-4fb9-bca8-f5ee213fa710]].
years.xp: Magic Circle had an LP due by summer. Battle Ruins was studio-only, Stone Dagger needed practice time, and Mind Eraser played about once every five years. The Rival Mob had no label for the new 7" yet.

eras.title: Still pressing it
eras.text: No new songs, but Mob Justice stayed in print. Revelation kept pressing it, in formats the label rarely uses.

years.h: A picture disc, only the third in Revelation's history
years.p: Mob Justice gets a picture disc repress. The two before it were Shai Hulud records.
years.xp: Hardcore Punk Wiki calls it "only the 3th picture disc ever on the label." The earlier ones were Shai Hulud's That Within Blood Ill-Tempered (2003) and A Profound Hatred of Man (2006).

years.h: Mob Justice comes back on goldenrod vinyl
years.p: A limited goldenrod reissue is listed, thirteen years after the album first came out.
